facts.text: East Cleveland is home to General Electric's historic Nela Park, the world's first industrial park, still operating as GE Lighting headquarters.
The East Cleveland Public Library, opened in 1916 with a donation from Andrew Carnegie, sits on land given by the Rockefellers.
About a third of Greater Cleveland Regional Transit Authority bus routes start or end in East Cleveland, making it a major public‑transport hub.
Huron Hospital, a Cleveland Clinic satellite, was the only Level‑II trauma center between MetroHealth and Hillcrest Hospital until it closed in 2011.
East Cleveland still houses 18 of Cleveland’s original 'Millionaire’s Row' homes, a rarity compared to only six left in Cleveland itself.
When East Cleveland incorporated in 1911, its charter included women's suffrage—an unheard‑of provision east of the Mississippi.
